overview: The API gateway runs the limiter as middleware. Token buckets per API key live in a Redis cluster and are refilled lazily inside a Lua script (atomic read-modify-write). Over-limit → 429 with Retry-After.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative fleet: 20 gateway instances, shared limit 100 requests/s/subject.
estimation.result: One coordinated state key enforces the intended global quota.
estimation.implication: Shard by subject/policy, use atomic scripts and account for hot-subject contention.

components.rationale: Keep validation and durable state in services; retry only according to the API contract.

components.purpose: Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for rate limiter.
components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.

components.purpose: Token bucket per API key via Lua script; 429 + Retry-After; fail open on Redis errors
components.rationale: Keep business invariants in the owning service; reject malformed or excessive traffic before expensive work.

components.purpose: Bucket state: tokens + last_refill, atomic Lua
components.rationale: Specify TTL and update strategy; durable state remains elsewhere unless an atomic admission decision explicitly depends on this store.

components.purpose: Per-tier limits, cached in gateway memory
components.rationale: Choose keys and indexes from the documented access patterns; replicas provide availability, not conflict-free arbitrary writes.

components.purpose: Implement the owned APIs and coordinate state transitions for rate limiter.
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

accessPatterns: Check and consume quota atomically on every protected request.
constraints: Use one Lua transaction for read/compute/write/expiry; hash-tag keys that must be updated together.

apiDetails.purpose: Decide whether one request may reach the backend.
apiDetails.rationale: Gateway middleware may invoke this internally; the separate limiter variant exposes the same internal contract. Define whether retries consume quota again.

apiDetails.purpose: Example backend endpoint protected by the limiter.
apiDetails.rationale: The backend executes only after the admission decision; use a coarse emergency local cap during shared-store outages.

flows.title: Allow or reject at the gateway

steps.title: API clients → LB → API Gateway → Redis cluster
steps.explanation: Read/refill/consume token-bucket state in one Lua operation. A denied request returns 429 with Retry-After.

steps.title: API Gateway → Backend API
steps.explanation: Only the allowed branch executes the protected backend.

steps.title: API Gateway → Rules DB
steps.explanation: Cache versioned limiter policies outside the per-request hot path.

steps.title: API Gateway → Redis cluster
steps.explanation: If Redis times out, apply the endpoint-specific fail-open/closed policy and emergency local cap.

failureCases.scenario: The shared counter store is unreachable
failureCases.handling: Choose fail-open for availability-oriented reads with a local emergency cap; fail-closed for expensive or sensitive operations. Bound the decision timeout and return a documented retry response.

alternatives: Use gateway token buckets for burst allowance and fewer hops. Use a dedicated sliding-window limiter for centralized policy and smoother quotas, accepting another decision hop. Define outage behavior per endpoint.
